card.procedure: 1) Identify the exact dosing decision the stem asks about (initial dose, adjustment, adequacy, timing). 2) Retrieve spans that state the dose or adjustment rule together with the patient condition it depends on. 3) Check whether the patient's stated condition (renal, hepatic, pregnancy, age, weight, indication) matches the condition in the span. 4) Treat an indication span as support for use and a contraindication or precaution span as opposition; do not invert polarity. 5) If no span ties a dose to the patient's condition, do not eliminate an option for that reason alone; fall back to condition-based evidence and state the matching span.
card.counterexample_explanation: The insulin case succeeded because the dose-reduction question was answered by matching the patient's situation (hypoglycemia-prone circumstances) to the condition-dependent dosing rule, not by preferring whichever option mentioned a number. card.name: interaction_pair_scope_check
card.exclude_reason: Applies only when the stem asks about a drug-drug or drug-condition interaction; interaction wording alone does not establish that any option is unsafe, and unknown facts never imply safety.
card.procedure: 1) Name the exact pair the stem asks about: which agent with which co-medication or condition. 2) Retrieve spans that name both members of that pair. 3) Classify each span: indication or administration detail supports use; contraindication, warning, or precaution opposes use. 4) Do not invert polarity, and do not treat a missing pair span as eliminating an option. 5) Select the option whose retrieved span matches the patient's stated co-medication or condition; if no span names the pair, fall back to condition-based evidence and say so.
card.counterexample_explanation: The cutaneous-candidiasis case succeeded because the chosen agent was matched to the patient's actual interacting cardiac medication, so the interaction span supported rather than filtered the answer. The levothyroxine case succeeded because the absorption-timing interaction was tied to the specific co-administered mineral, not to interaction wording in general. Preserving these means the step must keep interaction spans as pair-specific evidence and must not convert the mere presence of an interaction question into a preference for, or elimination of, any option.
